summary_ko: macOS 데스크톱 모양의 포트폴리오를 React·NestJS·PostgreSQL 로 다시 만들어, 메모 앱에서 바로 쓰는 블로그와 로그인 없는 방문자 기능, SSH 외에는 포트를 열지 않는 무료 서버 운영까지 혼자 구축했습니다.
summary_en: Rebuilt a macOS-desktop portfolio with React, NestJS and PostgreSQL: a blog written in place in the Notes app, sign-up-free visitor features, and a free server run with no open port except SSH — all solo.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-01.jpg.script: MacFolio 를 소개하겠습니다. MacFolio 는 웹 브라우저에서 동작하는 macOS 데스크톱 모양의 포트폴리오입니다. 화면 아래 Dock 에서 앱을 열고, 창을 옮기거나 크기를 바꿀 수 있으며, 메모 앱을 열면 블로그 글을 읽을 수 있습니다. 휴대폰으로 접속하면 같은 내용이 iOS 홈 화면 모양으로 바뀝니다. 2024년 8월에 시작해 2026년 10월까지 기획과 디자인, 프론트엔드와 백엔드, 서버 운영을 혼자 맡았습니다.

en.script: Let me introduce MacFolio, a portfolio shaped like a macOS desktop that runs in the web browser. You open apps from the Dock at the bottom, move and resize windows, and open the Notes app to read the blog. On a phone, the same content turns into an iOS home screen. From August 2024 to October 2026 I handled planning, design, frontend, backend and server operations on my own.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-02.jpg.script: 2024년에 만든 첫 버전은 보기만 하는 정적 사이트였습니다. Create React App 위에 화면을 모아 둔 형태였는데, CRA 는 2025년 2월에 지원이 종료되었습니다. 관리자 비밀번호는 Firebase 에 저장했는데, 보안 규칙이 열려 있어서 누구나 평문으로 읽을 수 있는 상태였습니다. 창과 Dock 은 있었지만 글을 쓰거나 고칠 수는 없었습니다. 그래서 2026년 9월, Vite 와 NestJS, PostgreSQL 모노레포로 처음부터 다시 만들었습니다. 겉모습은 macOS 그대로 두고, 안쪽은 실제로 운영하는 서비스로 만드는 것이 목표였습니다.

en.script: The first version, built in 2024, was a static site you could only look at. It was a set of screens on Create React App, which was deprecated in February 2025. The admin password was stored in Firebase with open security rules, so anyone could read it in plain text. It had windows and a Dock, but no way to write or edit anything. So in September 2026 I rebuilt it from scratch as a Vite, NestJS and PostgreSQL monorepo. The goal was to keep the macOS look and turn the inside into a service that actually runs.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-03.jpg.script: 개발 과정을 시간순으로 정리했습니다. 2024년 8월의 첫 커밋은 빌드 도구 없이 HTML, CSS, JavaScript 파일 세 개로 만든 화면이었습니다. 10월에 Create React App 과 TypeScript 로 옮기고 Express 서버와 MySQL 을 붙였다가 Google Cloud SQL 로 옮겼고, 12월에는 서버를 걷어 내고 Firebase 로 바꿨습니다. 2025년 3월에는 빌드 도구를 Vite 로 바꿨습니다. 본격적인 재구축은 2026년 9월 28일에 시작해, 다음 날 NestJS API 와 GitHub 로그인을, 그다음 날 Oracle VM 서버 배포를 마쳤습니다. 10월 18일에 리팩터링 일곱 단계를 마쳤고, 10월 19일 기준으로 브라우저 E2E 시험 486개와 단위 시험 659개를 갖추고 있습니다.

en.script: Here is the timeline. The first commit in August 2024 was a screen made of three HTML, CSS and JavaScript files with no build tool. In October it moved to Create React App and TypeScript, gained an Express server with MySQL, and then moved to Google Cloud SQL; in December the server was removed in favor of Firebase. In March 2025 the build tool switched to Vite. The real rebuild began on September 28, 2026; the NestJS API and GitHub login followed the next day, and the API was deployed on an Oracle VM the day after. The seven-step refactoring finished on October 18, and as of October 19 there are 486 browser end-to-end tests and 659 unit tests.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-04.jpg.script: 결과를 숫자로 보면 이렇습니다. 브라우저 E2E 시험 486개를 크롬, 아이폰, 안드로이드 세 화면에서 돌리고, 단위 시험 659개와 실제 PostgreSQL 에 연결한 API 시험 131개가 있습니다. API 경로 64개의 권한은 표 하나로 고정해 시험하고, 글쓰기처럼 데이터를 바꾸는 경로 33개에는 모두 요청 제한을 걸었습니다. 보안 점검에서 나온 7건 가운데 실제 취약점은 없었고, 서버에서 외부에 열어 둔 포트는 SSH 하나뿐입니다. 만든 과정은 사이트 안의 메모 앱에 200편이 넘는 글로 남겼습니다.

en.script: Here are the results in numbers. 486 browser end-to-end tests run on Chrome, iPhone and Android, alongside 659 unit tests and 131 API tests against a real PostgreSQL. Permissions for all 64 API routes are pinned in one table and tested, and all 33 routes that change data are rate-limited. Of the 7 findings from the security scan, none was a real vulnerability, and the only port the server exposes is SSH. The whole process is written up in more than 200 posts in the Notes app inside the site.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-05.jpg.script: 데스크톱에서는 macOS, 휴대폰에서는 iOS 모양이 됩니다. 앱마다 폴더를 하나씩 두고, manifest 파일 한 곳에서 Dock, Launchpad, 터미널의 open 명령, 휴대폰 홈 화면을 함께 관리합니다. 그래서 앱을 하나 추가하면 네 곳에 한 번에 나타납니다. 창은 옮기고, 크기를 바꾸고, 최소화할 수 있고, 메뉴 막대와 제어 센터, 휴대폰의 쓸어 넘기기도 지원합니다. 레이아웃은 화면 폭이 아니라 창 폭을 기준으로 바뀌기 때문에, 데스크톱에서 창을 좁히면 그 창 안이 휴대폰 화면처럼 바뀝니다. 글과 프로젝트마다 고유한 주소가 있어서 링크 하나로 그 화면을 바로 열 수 있습니다.

en.script: It looks like macOS on a desktop and like iOS on a phone. Each app has its own folder, and a single manifest file manages the Dock, Launchpad, the terminal's open command and the phone's home screen together, so a new app appears in all four places at once. Windows can be moved, resized and minimized, and there is a menu bar, a Control Center and swipe gestures on the phone. The layout follows the window width rather than the screen width, so narrowing a window on the desktop turns its contents into the phone layout. Every post and project has its own URL, so a single link opens that screen directly.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-06.jpg.script: 창 안의 앱들은 모양만 흉내 낸 것이 아니라 실제로 동작합니다. Finder 에서는 이력서 PDF 와 그림을 미리보기로 열고, 새 폴더를 만들거나 이름을 바꾸고 끌어서 옮길 수 있으며, 파일은 Cloudflare R2 에 저장됩니다. 메일 앱은 Resend 를 통해 실제로 메일을 보내고, Turnstile 로 사람인지 확인하며, IP 하나당 하루 다섯 통으로 제한합니다. 사진 앱은 프로젝트 정보로 앨범을 자동으로 만들고, 날씨 앱은 키가 필요 없는 Open-Meteo 를 씁니다. 시스템 설정에서는 코드를 고치지 않고 프로필과 프로젝트를 편집하고, API 문서 앱은 코드에서 뽑은 명세를 보여 주며 실제 코드와 어긋나면 CI 가 실패합니다.

en.script: The apps inside the windows are not just look-alikes; they actually work. Finder opens the résumé PDF and images in Preview, and lets you create, rename and drag folders, with files stored in Cloudflare R2. The Mail app really sends mail through Resend, checks for humans with Turnstile, and allows five messages per IP per day. Photos builds albums automatically from project data, and Weather uses Open-Meteo, which needs no API key. System Settings edits the profile and projects without touching code, and the API Docs app shows a spec generated from the code; if the two drift apart, CI fails.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-07.jpg.script: 메모 앱이 곧 블로그입니다. 관리자로 로그인하면 글을 읽던 화면이 그대로 편집기로 바뀌어서, 보이는 모습 그대로 글을 고칠 수 있습니다. 편집기는 Milkdown 과 ProseMirror 로 만들었고, 글은 Markdown 으로 저장해 저장소의 글 파일과 서버의 글이 같은 형식을 씁니다. 한 행에 게시본과 임시 저장본을 함께 두기 때문에, 고치는 동안에도 방문자는 게시본을 보고, 게시할 때마다 버전 기록이 남으며, 예약 게시도 할 수 있습니다. 게시한 글에는 제목과 본문이 있어야 한다는 규칙은 화면에서만 확인하지 않고 데이터베이스의 CHECK 제약으로 한 번 더 지킵니다.

en.script: The Notes app is the blog. When the admin signs in, the reading view itself becomes the editor, so posts are edited exactly as they appear. The editor is built with Milkdown and ProseMirror, and posts are stored as Markdown, so the files in the repository and the posts on the server share one format. Each row keeps both the published version and the draft, so visitors keep seeing the published post during edits, every publish leaves a revision, and posts can be scheduled. Rules such as 'a published post needs a title and a body' are checked not only on screen but again by a database CHECK constraint.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-08.jpg.script: 방문자는 로그인하지 않고 메시지와 댓글을 남길 수 있습니다. 이름이나 비밀번호를 입력받지 않고, 방문자 쿠키가 부지런한 판다 같은 이름을 자동으로 붙여 줍니다. 서버에는 원래 값을 저장하지 않습니다. 토큰과 IP 는 HMAC 으로, 세션은 SHA-256 해시로만 저장합니다. 그래서 내가 쓴 글은 같은 브라우저에서만 지울 수 있습니다. 데이터를 바꾸는 경로 33개에는 같은 방식의 요청 제한을 걸었고, 필요하면 Turnstile 로 사람인지 한 번 더 확인합니다.

en.script: Visitors can leave messages and comments without signing in. No name or password is asked; a visitor cookie assigns a playful animal name instead. The server never stores the original values: tokens and IPs are kept only as HMACs, and sessions only as SHA-256 hashes. That is why your own posts can be deleted only from the same browser. All 33 routes that change data share the same rate limit, and when needed, Turnstile adds a check that the visitor is human.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-09.jpg.script: 방문자 분석도 직접 만들었습니다. 쿠키를 쓰지 않고, 날짜와 IP, 브라우저 정보를 합쳐 만든 HMAC 값으로 하루 순방문자를 셉니다. 날짜가 계산에 들어가기 때문에 날이 바뀌면 같은 사람을 이어서 추적할 수 없습니다. 원래 IP 는 저장하지 않고, 가린 IP 는 7일, 방문 기록은 90일 동안만 보관합니다. 결과는 '활동 상태 보기' 앱에서 개요, 유입 경로, 많이 연 앱과 글, 지역과 기기, 실시간 다섯 탭으로 보여 주고, 그래프는 라이브러리 없이 SVG 로 그렸습니다. 합계는 방문자에게도 공개하고, 상세 주소와 UTM 정보, 실시간 현황은 관리자에게만 보이도록 서버에서 구분합니다.

en.script: I also built the visitor analytics myself. Without cookies, daily unique visitors are counted with an HMAC of the date, IP and browser information. Because the date is part of the calculation, the same person cannot be followed from one day to the next. The original IP is never stored; masked IPs are kept for 7 days and visit events for 90. The Activity Monitor app shows the results in five tabs: overview, referrers, top apps and posts, region and device, and real time, with charts drawn in plain SVG without a library. Totals are public to visitors, while detailed URLs, UTM data and real-time views are admin-only, separated on the server.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-10.jpg.script: 전체 구성입니다. 프론트엔드는 Cloudflare Workers 에서 정적 파일로 제공하고, API 는 Oracle 의 무료 VM 위에서 Docker Compose 로 NestJS 와 PostgreSQL 을 실행합니다. 서버 안의 cloudflared 가 Cloudflare 쪽으로 먼저 연결을 맺기 때문에, 80번과 443번 포트를 열지 않아도 요청이 서버에 도착합니다. 그래서 외부에 열어 둔 포트는 관리용 SSH 하나뿐입니다. 프론트엔드와 API 가 같은 사이트의 하위 도메인이라 로그인 쿠키도 그대로 함께 쓸 수 있습니다. 코드를 GitHub 에 병합하면 Actions 의 검사를 통과한 커밋만 서버에 배포됩니다.

en.script: Here is the overall architecture. The frontend is served as static files from Cloudflare Workers, and the API runs NestJS and PostgreSQL with Docker Compose on a free Oracle VM. Because cloudflared inside the server opens the connection to Cloudflare first, requests reach the server without opening ports 80 or 443, so the only exposed port is SSH for administration. The frontend and the API are subdomains of the same site, so the login cookie works across both. When code is merged on GitHub, only commits that pass the Actions checks are deployed to the server.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-11.jpg.script: 관리자가 아니면 편집 버튼이 보이지 않지만, 이것은 화면에서 감춘 것일 뿐입니다. 실제로 수정을 막는 것은 서버의 권한 검사입니다. 모든 요청마다 AdminGuard 가 데이터베이스의 세션을 확인하고, 바뀔 수 있는 이름 대신 GitHub 의 숫자 ID 로 관리자를 판별합니다. API 경로 64개와 각 경로의 권한 검사를 표 하나로 고정해 두어서, 새 경로에 검사를 빠뜨리면 시험이 실패합니다. Semgrep 규칙 266개로 점검한 결과 7건이 나왔지만 실제 취약점은 없었고, gitleaks 로 커밋 791개에 비밀 값이 섞이지 않았는지도 확인했습니다. 그 밖에 보안 헤더, iframe sandbox, Markdown 스크립트 삽입 시험, 업로드 사진의 위치 정보 제거, 로그의 비밀 값 가리기를 적용했습니다.

en.script: Non-admins don't see the edit button, but that only hides it on screen; what actually blocks changes is the server's permission check. On every request, AdminGuard checks the session in the database and identifies the admin by a numeric GitHub ID rather than a name that can change. All 64 API routes and their permission checks are pinned in one table, so leaving the check off a new route fails the tests. A Semgrep scan with 266 rules produced 7 findings, none of them real vulnerabilities, and gitleaks confirmed that no secrets were mixed into 791 commits. On top of that: security headers, iframe sandboxing, Markdown script-injection tests, stripping location data from uploaded photos, and masking secrets in logs.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-12.jpg.script: 배포는 검사를 모두 통과한 커밋만 나갑니다. 포맷, 린트, 타입, 단위 시험, 빌드를 거친 뒤, 실제 PostgreSQL 에 연결한 API 시험과 브라우저 E2E 시험까지 통과해야 합니다. Playwright 시험은 가짜 API 를 끼워 로그인부터 글쓰기, 게시까지 확인하고, 블로그에 쓰는 스크린샷도 같은 코드로 찍습니다. 병합에서 배포까지 15분이 걸렸는데 그중 E2E 가 8분에서 9분을 차지해서, E2E 를 여섯 칸으로 나눠 동시에 돌리고 PR 에서 이미 통과한 같은 코드는 다시 돌리지 않도록 했습니다. 서버는 Actions 에서 만든 이미지를 바꿔 끼우기만 하고, 헬스 체크가 실패하면 자동으로 이전 버전으로 되돌립니다. 이 되돌리기는 일부러 깨진 이미지를 올려 실제로 확인했습니다.

en.script: Only commits that pass every check are deployed. After format, lint, types, unit tests and build, they must also pass API tests against a real PostgreSQL and browser end-to-end tests. The Playwright tests plug in a fake API and verify everything from sign-in to writing and publishing, and the same code takes the screenshots used in the blog. Going from merge to deploy took 15 minutes, 8 to 9 of them in end-to-end tests, so the tests were split into six parallel shards, and code that already passed in a pull request is not run again. The server only swaps in the image built by Actions and rolls back automatically if the health check fails; I verified that rollback by deploying a deliberately broken image.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-13.jpg.script: 서버는 Oracle 의 무료 VM 에서 운영합니다. 이 VM 은 7일 동안 CPU 와 네트워크 사용률이 20% 아래로 머물면 회수될 수 있어서, 1분마다 사용률을 재고 위험해지면 메일로 알림을 받습니다. GitHub Actions 가 10분마다 서버 상태와 첫 화면을 확인하고, 실패하면 30초 간격으로 세 번 다시 확인합니다. 로그는 컨테이너마다 10MB 파일 세 개까지만 남겨 디스크가 차지 않게 했습니다. 데이터베이스는 매일 백업해 서버에 7일, R2 에 30일 보관하고, 백업을 별도 데이터베이스에 되살려 글 수가 같은지까지 확인했습니다. 메뉴 막대의 Wi-Fi 자리에는 서버 응답 상태를, 배터리 자리에는 관리자에게는 회수 위험을, 방문자에게는 방문 추이를 보여 줍니다.

en.script: The server runs on Oracle's free VM. That VM can be reclaimed if CPU and network usage stay below 20% for seven days, so usage is measured every minute and an email alert goes out when it gets risky. GitHub Actions checks the server health and the home screen every 10 minutes, retrying three times at 30-second intervals on failure. Logs are capped at three 10 MB files per container so the disk never fills up. The database is backed up daily, kept for 7 days on the server and 30 days in R2, and a backup was restored into a separate database to confirm the post count matched. In the menu bar, the Wi-Fi spot shows the server's response status, and the battery spot shows the reclaim risk to the admin and the visit trend to visitors.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-14.jpg.script: 기능을 빠르게 붙이면서 쌓인 중복은 일곱 단계로 정리했습니다. 화면마다 응답 타입을 손으로 다시 적던 것은 contracts 의 zod 스키마 하나로 모았습니다. fetch 를 쓰던 파일 22개는 client.ts 하나로 모아 346줄을 179줄로 줄였습니다. 창, 메모, 음악 로직은 React 밖의 desktop-core 로 옮겨서 React 와 DOM 없이 시험합니다. 스타일에서는 색 288곳과 글자 크기 645곳을 토큰으로 바꾸고, important 선언 72개를 정리했습니다. 4,600줄이던 메모 CSS 는 15개 파일로 나누고 빌드 결과가 같은지 확인했습니다. 린트 경고 185개와 순환 의존 2개는 0으로 만들고, 새 경고가 생기면 CI 가 막도록 했습니다.

en.script: The duplication that built up while shipping features quickly was cleaned up in seven steps. Response types that each screen retyped by hand now come from one zod schema in contracts. Twenty-two files that used fetch were consolidated into one client.ts, cutting 346 lines to 179. Window, Notes and music logic moved out of React into desktop-core and is tested without React or the DOM. In styles, 288 colors and 645 font sizes became tokens, and 72 important declarations were removed. The 4,600-line Notes stylesheet was split into 15 files, with the build output verified to be identical. The 185 lint warnings and two circular dependencies went to zero, and CI now blocks any new warning.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-15.jpg.script: 원인을 찾아 고친 문제 네 가지를 소개합니다. 첫째, 공통 버튼의 여백이 0이 되었습니다. CSS 층의 순서는 문서에서 처음 선언된 곳이 정하는데, 컴포넌트 CSS 가 먼저 불러와져 초기화 규칙이 이겼기 때문입니다. 층 순서 선언을 HTML 맨 앞으로 옮겨 고쳤습니다. 둘째, 배포 직후 메모 앱이 열리지 않았습니다. 열려 있던 탭이 이미 사라진 옛 파일을 요청했고, 없는 파일에도 index.html 이 정상 응답으로 1년 동안 캐시되었기 때문입니다. 없는 파일은 404 로 응답하게 하고 새로고침 안내를 띄웠습니다. 셋째, 서버가 켜져 있는데 연결할 수 없다고 표시되었는데, 미리보기 주소가 CORS 에 막혔고 브라우저가 막힘과 꺼짐을 같은 오류로 돌려주었기 때문입니다. 넷째, 한국어 뒤의 굵은 글씨가 깨지는 문제는 한국어에 맞춘 Markdown 플러그인으로 고쳤습니다.

en.script: Here are four problems I traced to their causes. First, the shared button lost its padding. CSS layer order is decided by the first declaration in the document, and because component CSS loaded first, the reset rule won; moving the layer-order declaration to the top of the HTML fixed it. Second, the Notes app failed to open right after a deploy. Open tabs requested old files that no longer existed, and missing files were answered with index.html as a success, cached for a year; missing files now return 404 and a reload prompt appears. Third, the server showed as unreachable while it was running, because CORS blocked the preview URL and the browser reported blocked and offline as the same error. Fourth, bold text breaking after Korean words was fixed with a Markdown plugin tuned for Korean.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-16.jpg.script: 빌드 도구는 Create React App 에서 Vite 로 옮겼습니다. 2025년 3월에 Vite 를 도입했고, 2026년 9월에 남아 있던 CRA 흔적을 정리한 뒤 같은 조건에서 다시 측정했습니다. 개발 서버 시작은 5.05초에서 0.58초로, 프로덕션 빌드는 6.33초에서 1.88초로 줄었습니다. 압축한 JS 번들은 138.2KB 에서 127.7KB 로, 설치 패키지는 1,438개에서 171개로 줄었습니다. 정리하는 과정에서 잘못된 배포 경로, 예전 환경 변수 이름, 빠진 의존성처럼 그동안 드러나지 않던 오류 네 건도 찾아 고쳤습니다.

en.script: The build tool moved from Create React App to Vite. Vite was introduced in March 2025, and in September 2026 the remaining CRA leftovers were cleaned up and everything was measured again under the same conditions. Dev-server startup dropped from 5.05 to 0.58 seconds, and the production build from 6.33 to 1.88 seconds. The compressed JS bundle went from 138.2 KB to 127.7 KB, and installed packages from 1,438 to 171. The cleanup also uncovered four errors that had gone unnoticed, such as a wrong deploy path, old environment variable names and missing dependencies.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-17.jpg.script: 돌아보면, 보기만 하던 모형을 서비스로 바꾸는 일은 화면 뒤를 만드는 일이었습니다. 이 과정에서 세 가지 원칙을 지켰습니다. 첫째, 고치기 전에 먼저 셌습니다. 공통 부품 후보 아홉 개를 따져 보니 실제로 필요한 것은 세 개였고, 쓰지 않는 CSS 후보 150개 가운데 실제로 지운 것은 아홉 개였습니다. 둘째, 리팩터링 뒤에는 결과가 같은지 확인했습니다. 빌드한 CSS 를 바이트 단위로, 화면은 계산된 스타일로 비교했습니다. 셋째, 동작이 바뀌는 보안 변경은 리팩터링과 섞지 않고 따로 냈습니다. 그 결과 권한은 서버가, 데이터 규칙은 DB 제약과 시험이 지키고, 검사를 통과한 커밋만 배포되는 구조가 되어 혼자서도 안전하게 고칠 수 있게 되었습니다. 다음 과제는 보류한 공통 부품 여섯 개와 이름이 없는 색 225곳을 정리하는 것입니다.

en.script: Looking back, turning a look-only mock-up into a service meant building what sits behind the screen. I kept to three principles. First, count before changing: of nine candidates for shared components, only three were really needed, and of 150 suspected unused CSS rules, only nine were actually removed. Second, confirm nothing changed after refactoring, comparing the built CSS byte by byte and screens by their computed styles. Third, ship behavior-changing security work separately from refactoring. As a result, the server guards permissions, database constraints and tests guard data rules, and only commits that pass the checks are deployed, so the project can be changed safely by one person. Next up: the six shared components put on hold and 225 colors that still have no name.

/content/works/macfolio/slide-18.jpg.script: 정리하면, MacFolio 는 겉모습은 macOS 이고 안쪽은 실제로 운영하는 서비스입니다. 브라우저 E2E 시험 486개가 화면을 지키고, API 경로 64개의 권한은 표 하나로 고정되어 있으며, 서버에서 외부에 열어 둔 포트는 SSH 하나뿐입니다. 만든 과정은 200편이 넘는 글로 사이트 안에 남겨 두었습니다. macfolio.hyeoniverse.com 에서 직접 Dock 을 열어 보시고, 소스 코드는 GitHub 에서 보실 수 있습니다. 들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

en.script: To sum up, MacFolio looks like macOS on the outside and is a service that actually runs on the inside. 486 browser end-to-end tests guard the screens, permissions for 64 API routes are pinned in one table, and the only port the server exposes is SSH. The whole process is kept in more than 200 posts inside the site. Open the Dock yourself at macfolio.hyeoniverse.com, and the source code is on GitHub. Thank you for listening.

content_en:
![MacFolio desktop: menu bar, Notes window, and the Dock below](/content/works/macfolio/desktop.jpg)

## At a Glance

| Item | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Period | 2024.08 – 2024.12 (prototype), 2026.09 – 2026.10 (rebuild) |
| Team | Solo |
| Role | Planning, design, frontend, backend, infrastructure, CI/CD |
| Scale | 486 browser E2E tests · 659 unit tests, permissions of 64 API routes pinned, 23 apps (18 built-in · 5 projects), 200+ dev-log posts (as of 2026-10-19) |
| Deployment | Cloudflare Workers (frontend), Oracle Cloud VM + Docker Compose + Cloudflare Tunnel (API) |
| Links | [macfolio.hyeoniverse.com](https://macfolio.hyeoniverse.com) · [API docs](https://macfolio-api.hyeoniverse.com/docs) |

> [!TIP]
> It looks exactly like macOS, but inside it is a service that really runs. The permissions of all 64 API routes are pinned by a single table test, the API runs on a free server with no open port except SSH, and the whole build process is recorded in more than 200 posts in the site's own Notes app.

## Overview

MacFolio is a portfolio that brings the macOS desktop to the web. You open apps from the Dock, drag windows by their title bars, and read the blog in the Notes app. Typing `about`, `skills` or `projects` in the terminal shows an introduction, and Safari and the project apps run my other deployed work right inside a window. On a phone it turns into an iOS home screen with widgets and a swipe-down Control Center.

The 2024 prototype, built with Create React App and Firebase, was a mock-up you could only look at. The admin password lived in Firebase with open security rules, so anyone could read it in plain text, and CRA was deprecated in February 2025. In September 2026 I rebuilt it as a Vite + NestJS + PostgreSQL monorepo with one goal: "macOS on the outside, a service that actually runs on the inside."

## Timeline

| When | What |
| --- | --- |
| 2024.08.27 | First commit: three HTML · CSS · JS files with no build tool |
| 2024.10 | Moved to Create React App and TypeScript, added an Express server with MySQL, then moved to Google Cloud SQL |
| 2024.12 | Removed the server and moved to Firebase Hosting and Realtime DB, React 19 |
| 2025.03 | Switched the build tool to Vite (CRA leftovers remained in the deploy setup) |
| 2026.09.28 | Rebuild started: Firebase removed, Cloudflare Workers deploy, monorepo, E2E tests 0 → 78 |
| 2026.09.29 | NestJS API and GitHub sign-in |
| 2026.09.30 | API deployed on an Oracle VM with Cloudflare Tunnel |
| 2026.10.18 | Seven-step refactoring completed |
| 2026.10.19 | 486 browser E2E tests · 659 unit tests · 131 API E2E tests |

## Key Features

- **Desktop and phone** Window dragging, resizing, minimizing and full screen, a menu bar, Launchpad and desktop icons. On a phone: an iOS home screen, Control Center, and Shortcuts in place of the terminal. The layout uses container queries based on the window width, not the screen width, so narrowing a window on the desktop turns its contents into the phone layout.
- **One app list** Each app is one folder, and a single `manifest.ts` is the source for the Dock, Launchpad, the terminal's `open` and the phone home screen. Adding an app makes it appear in all four places.
- **Notes = blog** Folder and gallery views, tags, search, find and replace. When the admin signs in, the reading view becomes the editor, with drafts, publishing, scheduling and revision history.
- **Visitor features** Feedback in the Messages app, blog comments and likes, all without signing in. A visitor cookie picks a playful name, and only the same browser can delete its posts.
- **Apps with URLs** Arriving at `/memo/<post>` or `/safari/<project>` opens that app on that screen, and the address bar follows the frontmost window.
- **Operations tools** Server status in the menu bar, cookie-free visitor analytics (Activity Monitor), résumé and document preview in Finder, and admin-uploaded wallpapers.

![The home screen on iPhone and Android](/content/works/macfolio/mobile-devices.jpg)

![The Notes editor: the reading view is the editor](/content/works/macfolio/memo-editor.jpg)

## Apps in the Windows

The apps are not just look-alikes; they actually work. There are 18 built-in apps and 5 project apps that run my deployed projects.

- **Finder** Browse four groups (documents, projects, blog, applications) like files. The résumé PDF and images open in Preview, and folders can be created, renamed and moved by dragging. Files live in Cloudflare R2 and a Worker serves them under `/files/`.
- **Mail** The server really sends mail through Resend, with the visitor's address as Reply-To. Turnstile checks for humans, and sending is limited to 5 messages per IP and 50 per site each day. The Sent mailbox is filtered on the server by an HMAC of the visitor cookie.
- **Photos** Albums are built automatically from project data: 65 photos and 5 videos from seven projects.
- **Weather** Uses Open-Meteo, which needs no API key. Because city search took 1 to 10 seconds, the built-in city list grew from 39 to 211.
- **System Settings** Edit the profile and projects without touching code, and turn Turnstile on or off separately for mail, comments and messages.
- **API Docs** Shows the OpenAPI spec generated from the API code with Scalar, and opens even when the server is down. If the spec drifts from the code, CI fails.
- **Project apps · Sprout Farm** HYEONIVERSE, NewPick, QRU, WTD and Sprout Farm run in windows through one component, including a Unity WebGL game in an iframe.

![Finder: the Documents folder](/content/works/macfolio/finder.jpg)

![Mail: the inbox](/content/works/macfolio/mail.jpg)

![Weather](/content/works/macfolio/weather.jpg)

![Photos: project albums](/content/works/macfolio/photos.jpg)

## Visitor Analytics

The visitor analytics are built in-house, with no third-party analytics tool.

- **Unique visitors without cookies** Daily unique visitors are counted with `HMAC(date + IP + User-Agent, secret key)`. Because the date is part of the hash, the same person cannot be followed from one day to the next. Weekly uniques are the sum of the daily counts.
- **Retention** The original IP is never stored. Masked IPs are kept for 7 days and events for 90 days; only the daily aggregates are kept long term.
- **Collection** Five event types (`visit` · `app` · `item` · `link` · `leave`) are batched every 5 seconds and sent with `sendBeacon`. Local addresses, browsers with GPC enabled, and the admin are not counted.
- **Activity Monitor** Five tabs (overview, referrers, apps and posts, region and device, real time) with ranges of today, 7, 30 and 90 days. Charts are plain SVG, drawn without a library.
- **Visibility** Totals and referrer groups are public to visitors; detailed URLs, UTM details and the real-time view are admin-only, separated on the server.
- **UTM** A combination table, a trend view and a link builder; UTM parameters are removed from the address bar once read.

![Activity Monitor: visits, unique visitors, app opens and average time on site](/content/works/macfolio/activity.jpg)

## Architecture

![Architecture: Cloudflare Workers, Tunnel, and cloudflared · NestJS · PostgreSQL on an Oracle VM](/content/works/macfolio/architecture.jpg)

- **Frontend** A React 19 SPA. Window management, Notes and music logic live in `packages/desktop-core`, which is tested without React or the DOM.
- **Backend** NestJS feature modules with Prisma 7 + PostgreSQL 17. Every input is checked against a DTO whitelist, and the screen and the server share one zod schema from `@macfolio/contracts` for response shapes.
- **Infrastructure** The frontend is served as static assets on Cloudflare Workers, and the API runs with Docker Compose on an Oracle Always Free VM. Because `cloudflared` opens the connection outward from inside the server, ports 80 and 443 stay closed, and since both are subdomains of the same site, the `SameSite=Lax` session cookie is shared.

## Technical Challenges

### Protecting admin rights on a static site

**Symptom** The prototype kept the admin password in Firebase with open security rules, so anyone could read it in plain text. The edit button was hidden from non-admins, but hiding a button did nothing to stop edits.

**Cause** A static site has no place to verify requests. Everything the browser holds is public.

**Fix** Verification moved to the server. The admin signs in with GitHub OAuth and is identified by a numeric ID instead of a username that can change. A `state` cookie blocks login CSRF; the session is an `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie valid for 12 hours, and the database stores only a SHA-256 hash of the token. `AdminGuard` checks the session against the database on every request, and a test that pins all 64 API routes and their permission checks in one table fails if a check is missing.

**Result** The edit button is only hidden on screen; what actually blocks changes is the server's permission check on every request. With no password involved, password hashing and reset features were no longer needed.

### Drafts and revisions for a blog you edit in place

**Symptom** Editing right in the reading view, as in Notes, is convenient, but every save went live immediately and could not be undone.

**Cause** Each post row held only one copy of the content, so "being edited" and "published" could not be separated.

**Fix** Each row keeps two copies, the published content and the draft, and every publish leaves a `PostRevision`. Rules such as "a published post needs a title and a body" cannot be expressed in the Prisma schema, so a CHECK constraint in the migration SQL enforces them again in the database. The Markdown posts in the repository stay as they are, and posts edited on the server take their place at the same URL.

![Draft and published states](/content/works/macfolio/drafts.jpg)

**Result** Edits stay in the draft until published. Publishing with a future date schedules the post, and earlier revisions can be restored.

### Posting without signing in, without storing the originals

**Symptom** Every message and comment asked for a name and password, and the server stored IPs as-is.

**Cause** A password was the only way to tell who owned a post.

**Fix** A visitor cookie token identifies the owner and also picks the display name. The server stores only HMACs of the token and IP and SHA-256 hashes of sessions. All 33 write routes share the same per-IP rate limit (`@RateLimit`), and Cloudflare Turnstile can be turned on in System Settings when needed.

![The Messages app](/content/works/macfolio/messages.jpg)

**Result** Visitors post without typing anything and can delete from the same browser. The server keeps no personal data that could be turned back into the original values.

### A free server with no exposed web ports

**Symptom** Free hosting such as Render slept after 15 minutes without requests and took about a minute to wake up, while running my own VM meant opening ports 80 and 443 and renewing certificates.

**Cause** Free platforms trade response time for less operational work, and self-hosting enlarges the attack surface.

**Fix** PostgreSQL, the API and cloudflared run together with Docker Compose on an Oracle Always Free VM. The compose file has no `ports` at all, and the only open port on the server is SSH. The API image is built for amd64 and arm64 in GitHub Actions and pushed to GHCR; the server only swaps images. If the health check fails it rolls back automatically, and I rehearsed the rollback by deploying a deliberately broken image.

**Result** The server never sleeps, costs nothing, and does not reveal its IP. Hardening lives in the `ops/audit.sh` script rather than a document, so it can be re-checked at any time.

### Ten days of duplication, cleaned up in seven steps

**Symptom** While features were added quickly, screens retyped response types by hand, 12 files each called `fetch`, `z-index` had 23 different values, `Memo.css` reached 4,166 lines, and ESLint showed 185 warnings.

**Cause** Every new feature meant changes in several places, and security settings differed from feature to feature.

**Fix** The work was split into seven steps: types → structure → shared foundation → components → styles → server → security. Steps 1 to 6 were not allowed to change behavior, so the built CSS was compared byte by byte and screens by computed styles to confirm identical results. Security pull requests that change behavior were never mixed with refactoring. Design tokens now cover 288 colors, 645 font sizes (8 names) and 239 corner radii (6 names), and 72 `!important` declarations were cleaned up.

**Result** Types come from one zod schema in contracts, server calls go through one `client.ts`, circular dependencies are at 0 (blocked by CI), design tokens fall into six groups, and ESLint warnings are at 0 (`--max-warnings 0`). The site gained CSP and iframe sandboxing, and 6 dependency vulnerabilities were fixed.

### The shared button that lost its padding

**Symptom** The shared `Button` rendered with 0px padding.

**Cause** The order of CSS layers (`@layer`) is decided by the first declaration in the document. Component CSS loaded first and changed the layer order, so `* { padding: 0 }` in the reset layer won.

**Fix** The layer-order declaration moved to the very start of an inline `<style>` in `index.html`.

**Result** The padding returned to `5px 14px`, and the layer order no longer depends on which CSS loads first.

### The Notes app that would not open right after a deploy

**Symptom** Right after a deploy, open tabs showed "Something went wrong in the memo app."

**Cause** Open tabs requested old code files that the deploy had removed. Requests for missing files were answered with `index.html`, a 200 status and a one-year cache, so the browser tried to run HTML as code and failed.

**Fix** A Worker that handles only missing paths now returns 200 for app URLs and 404 for code files, and an alert suggests reloading when a code file cannot be loaded.

**Result** Wrong responses are no longer cached after a deploy, and a single reload brings the new version.

### "Cannot connect" while the server was running

**Symptom** On PR preview URLs, the menu bar showed "Cannot connect to the server" even though the server was healthy.

**Cause** CORS did not allow the preview URL, and the browser's `fetch` reports a CORS block and a server that is down as the same `TypeError`.

**Fix** Preview URLs are allowed by CORS without cookies, and a second `no-cors` request tells a block apart from an outage.

**Result** The status indicator matches the real server state, and previews cannot use the admin API.

### Bold text breaking after Korean words

**Symptom** When a Korean particle directly followed bold text, as in `**취소(cancelled)**가`, the asterisks showed up literally.

**Cause** CommonMark's rule for closing emphasis does not fit Korean, where particles attach directly to words.

**Fix** `remark-cjk-friendly` was applied to the three reading views and to the editor (reading and writing).

**Result** Bold text inside Korean sentences renders as intended.

## Operations and Monitoring

- **Reclaim watch** An Oracle Always Free VM (1 GB) can be reclaimed if CPU p95, network and memory usage all stay under 20% for seven days. `/proc` is read every minute; under 20% counts as risky and under 30% as a warning, and risky states send an email (the same alert at most once every three days).
- **Uptime checks** GitHub Actions checks `/health` and the home screen every 10 minutes, retrying three times at 30-second intervals on failure.
- **Log caps** Logs are limited to three 10 MB files (30 MB) per container so the disk never fills up.
- **Backups** A daily `pg_dump` is kept for 7 days on the server and 30 days in R2, with failures reported through healthchecks.io. A backup was restored into a separate database to confirm the post count matched the live one.
- **Menu bar icons** The Wi-Fi spot shows the server response status checked every 30 seconds; the battery spot shows the reclaim risk to the admin and the visit trend versus the previous week to visitors.

## Testing and Deployment

Branch, commit and PR rules are enforced by a `conventions` check in CI rather than left in a document. Every PR and main push runs format → lint → type check → unit tests → build → API E2E against a real PostgreSQL → browser E2E, and only commits that pass `check` are deployed to Cloudflare Workers. Every PR gets a preview URL, where CORS allows reading only and no admin cookie is issued.

Playwright verifies sign-in, writing and publishing on three screens (desktop Chrome, iPhone and Android) with a fake API (`page.route`), and the same code takes the screenshots for the README and the blog. As of October 19, 2026 there are 486 browser E2E tests, 659 unit tests and 131 API E2E tests.

Going from merge to deploy took 15 minutes, 8 to 9 of them in E2E. E2E was split into six parallel shards, and code that already passed in a PR (a commit with the same `HEAD^{tree}`) is not run again on main.

Security checks use Semgrep (266 rules), pnpm audit, osv-scanner and gitleaks. Of the 7 Semgrep findings, none was a real vulnerability, and gitleaks scanned 791 commits to confirm no secrets had slipped in. The site sends five security headers including CSP, with E2E failing on any violation, and uploaded photos have their EXIF data removed except for orientation.

The whole process is recorded in more than 200 posts in the Notes app's dev-log folder inside the site.

## CRA → Vite Migration

The build tool switched to Vite in March 2025; on the first day of the September 2026 rebuild, the remaining CRA leftovers were cleaned up and everything was measured again under the same conditions.

| Item | CRA | Vite |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dev server start | 5.05 s | 0.58 s |
| Production build | 6.33 s | 1.88 s |
| JS bundle (gzip) | 138.2 KB | 127.7 KB |
| Installed packages | 1,438 | 171 |

The cleanup also fixed four errors that had gone unnoticed: the deploy path still pointed to CRA's `build/`, `REACT_APP_` environment variable names remained, the `@vitejs/plugin-react` setup was missing, and `react-dom` and `typescript` were missing from the dependencies.

## Looking Back

Turning a look-only mock-up into a service meant building what sits behind the screen. The server checks permissions on every request, database constraints and tests check data rules a second time, and only commits that pass the checks are deployed.

The work followed three principles. First, count before changing: of nine candidates for shared components, three were really needed, and of 150 suspected unused CSS rules, nine were actually removed. Second, after refactoring, confirm the result is identical through the build output and computed styles. Third, ship security changes that alter behavior separately from refactoring.

Remaining work: the six shared components put on hold, and 225 hex colors that still have no name.
